entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded, normatively conferred relationship whereby a legal or social rule attaches an obligation to a specific agent. This fits BFO Role (BFO_0000023): it inheres in the agent-bearer, is externally grounded (by norms, contracts, statutes), and is realizable in processes of compliance or enforcement. It is not a Disposition because its ground is external (social/legal recognition), not an intrinsic physical structure of the bearer. The existing class LegalObligation is already typed as BFO_0000023; AgentObligationBinding is more specific, denoting the binding relation-as-role rather than the obligation content itself, and warrants a distinct class. It is modeled as a class (common noun denoting a kind) rather than an individual.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a species of LegalObligation: every instance of an agent-obligation binding is a legal obligation role inhering in an agent. Placing it as a subclass preserves the existing hierarchy under BFO_0000023 and avoids duplication.

open_questions: Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended as a dyadic relation (between a specific agent-individual and an obligation-individual), or as a kind/class of role that any agent may bear? If the former, it may be better modeled as an individual object property assertion rather than a new class.

Should AgentObligationBinding be restricted to legal obligations (inhering in legal persons) or does it extend to moral or contractual obligations as well? This affects whether it subclasses LegalObligation or sits directly under BFO_0000023.
Is there a specific process (e.g., contract formation, statute enactment) in which this role is realized? If so, a BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation to that process class would be appropriate.

Is 'binding' here intended to mark the obligatory force (deontic modality) as distinct from a mere obligation-as-content? If so, a separate treatment via a NormOntologicalCondition or Disposition subclass may be warranted.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the normative tie that attaches an obligation to a bearer-agent. In BFO 2020, such a tie is best classified as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a material entity (the agent), is externally grounded (by law, contract, or social norms), and is realizable in processes of compliance, enforcement, or adjudication. It differs from Disposition (BFO_0000016), which is internally grounded in the physical or constitutive structure of the bearer. A new class AgentObligationBinding is proposed under BFO_0000023 as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation, capturing the binding aspect as a role-kind rather than an obligation-content. Open questions are raised about whether this should be an individual relation or a class, and about the scope of the obligation type.
